notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 58 this time. My first attempt to read the commentary pages failed, and my tools were then cut off for the rest of this turn. I didn't get to read any pages from the approved sites. You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a link for every point, so I haven't written anything from memory.

These are the pages I had lined up to read first:
- Enduring Word (David Guzik): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-58/
- Gill: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/58.htm
- Ellicott: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/58.htm
- Pulpit Commentary: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/psalms/58.htm
- Barnes: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes/psalms/58.htm
- Wesley's Notes: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wesley/psalms/58.htm
- Augustine on this psalm (Catholic): https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1801058.htm. Catholic Bibles number it Psalm 57, so I'll check this is the right page.

After those, I'd look for:
- Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (Baptist).
- The NET Bible notes on the difficult Hebrew in verses 7–9, for modern scholarship.
- Articles on Got Questions, Desiring God, The Gospel Coalition and Ligonier about "imprecatory psalms": prayers asking God to punish enemies, like verses 6–10. These are where the traditions are most likely to differ.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll do the research and write the verse-by-verse notes with a link for every point.
